answer: Invariant: no fresh key inherits trust without a costly, decay-tested climb. First condition: entry requires ascending a difficulty ridge over a public, timestamped terrace of recent work, so minting a thousand keys costs a thousand real climbs, not one signature. Second condition: each key's standing decays unless its signal is independently corroborated by neighbors outside its own terrace cohort, so clones cannot vouch for each other. A sybil swarm pays the ridge per key and still starves on corroboration.
